name: Economics, Control, Information, and Process Map

positioning.oneLineSummary: Classifies each financing term by who it affects, in which state, and through economics, control, information, retention, or process.
positioning.productLabel: Venture Deal Rights Map — based on Feld and Mendelson's public Venture Deals materials
notAClaimOf: economics and control being mutually exclusive
term labels being sufficient to determine outcomes
a short term sheet capturing every definitive-document right

attribution.display: Based on Brad Feld and Jason Mendelson's public Venture Deals materials

neutralParaphrase: Start by separating terms that affect financial payoff from terms that affect decision authority, then add information, retention, and closing-process effects. For every term, record the rights holder, affected class, triggering event, threshold, duration, exceptions, and downstream calculation rather than assigning a generic favorable or unfavorable label.

locator.value: Opening sections: economics as return effects and control as affirmative or veto mechanisms
Chapters 4-9: overview, economic terms, control terms, other terms, convertible debt, and capitalization table
Complete term-sheet series index and not-legal-advice disclaimer

requiredConditions: The exact document version and jurisdiction are known.
Each right has an owner, affected class, trigger, threshold, duration, and exception.
Signed and executed documents override summaries and templates.
Economic calculations and legal enforceability are handled by separate services and counsel.

requiredEvidence.description: Signed term sheet and all relevant definitive financing, charter, side-letter, employment, and equity documents.
Clause-level inventory of right, owner, class, trigger, threshold, duration, exception, and linked calculation.
Entity jurisdiction, governing law, document date, amendments, waivers, and current effect.

decisionQuestions: Who owns each right and which class or person is burdened?
Does it change payoff, ownership, vote, veto, information, retention, or process?
What threshold, sunset, waiver, or exception applies?
Which rights interact or conflict in the same state?
Which deterministic service and counsel review are required?
positiveSignals: Every material clause maps to a state, owner, and effect.
Economic and control consequences are separately modeled.
Sunsets, waivers, thresholds, and side letters are visible.
Counsel confirms ambiguous or jurisdiction-specific clauses.
redFlags: Terms are scored by label alone.
A template substitutes for signed documents.
Economics and control effects are collapsed into one score.
Side letters, amendments, or class-specific rights are absent.
The system offers legal enforceability conclusions.
disconfirmingEvidence: Definitive documents differ from the term sheet.
An amendment, waiver, conversion, or sunset terminated the right.
A side letter changes one investor's rights.
Jurisdiction makes the assumed mechanism unavailable or different.
Two clauses create a conflict not represented by the simple label.
contraindications: Do not interpret rights without exact clause locators.
Do not apply US conventions to another jurisdiction without counsel mapping.
Do not make a legal conclusion.
Do not issue Invest Candidate from the rights map.

instructions: Inventory the complete document set and versions.
Extract each right with clause locator, owner, trigger, threshold, duration, exception, and affected state.
Route numeric and governance effects to deterministic services.
Display conflicts, unknowns, and counsel questions.

sourceReliability.low: Only a verbal summary or outdated term sheet exists.
sourceReliability.medium: Signed documents exist but amendments, side letters, or counsel review are incomplete.
sourceReliability.high: Executed documents, amendments, cap table, and counsel-confirmed inventory reconcile.

evidenceStrength.low: Labels are known but triggers and effects are not.
evidenceStrength.medium: Most rights and effects are mapped with limited ambiguity.
evidenceStrength.high: Every material right is clause-linked and state-tested.

evidenceCoverage.low: Only valuation and ownership are covered.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Economics and control are covered but process, side letters, or retention are partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: All economics, control, information, retention, process, amendments, and conflicts are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: Jurisdiction or instrument does not fit the public doctrine.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: US-style structure exists with custom clauses.
applicabilityConfidence.high: The financing uses a well-defined US venture-document structure.

judgmentConfidence.medium: A rights map is usable with counsel flags.
judgmentConfidence.high: The map is complete and ready for deterministic analysis.

promotionRequirements: Complete fourth-edition and current NVCA mapping.
Validate clause extraction and state routing on golden documents.
empiricalQualifications: Term usage and drafting vary by stage, jurisdiction, cycle, and counsel.
A clause can have indirect effects beyond its primary category.
Signed documents can diverge materially from negotiation summaries.

rights.notes: Public author materials are neutrally paraphrased; no legal advice is provided.

openIssues: Define clause-level rights schema and current NVCA mapping.
